text: 脱裤子打老虎——既不要脸，又不要命
pinyin: tuō kù zi dǎ lǎo hǔ —— jì bù yào liǎn, yòu bù yào mìng
literal: take off · trousers · fight · tiger — both · not · want · face, also · not · want · life
natural: fighting a tiger with one's trousers down

meaning.en: Fighting a tiger with no trousers on; someone who has neither shame nor fear of death, or is utterly reckless.
meaning.zh: 脱了裤子去打老虎；比喻既不顾脸面，也不顾性命，豁出去了。

equivalents: throw caution and dignity to the wind

examples.zh: 他欠了赌债，现在脱裤子打老虎，什么都干得出来。
examples.en: He's in gambling debt and will stop at nothing.

examples.zh: 这种脱裤子打老虎的人，你惹不起。
examples.en: You can't afford to cross someone so reckless.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Vulgar; sometimes used of those who have lost all sense of shame.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。较粗俗，常指不要脸面、豁出去的人。

text: 剃头挑子——一头热
pinyin: tì tóu tiāo zi —— yī tóu rè
literal: barber · carrying pole — one · end · hot
natural: a barber's carrying-pole: only one end is hot

meaning.en: A travelling barber's pole has the stove at one end only; one side is keen while the other is indifferent.
meaning.zh: 旧时剃头匠的担子，一头是热水炉；比喻一方热心，另一方冷淡。

examples.zh: 他追了她三年，剃头挑子一头热。
examples.en: He chased her for three years, but only he was keen.

examples.zh: 合作不能剃头挑子一头热，得双方都投入。
examples.en: A partnership can't be one-sided; both sides must commit.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The pole of an old street barber carried a small stove at one end and tools at the other. The saying is also written 剃头挑子一头热.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。旧时剃头匠的担子一头是炉子，一头是工具。也说“剃头挑子一头热”。

text: 太岁头上动土——找死
pinyin: tài suì tóu shàng dòng tǔ —— zhǎo sǐ
literal: Tai Sui · head · on · move · earth — seek · death
natural: digging earth on the head of Tai Sui

meaning.en: Breaking ground on the spot of the Grand Duke Jupiter spirit invites disaster; offending someone far too powerful.
meaning.zh: 在太岁神的方位上动土，必招灾祸；比喻冒犯强大的人，自找麻烦。

equivalents: beard the lion in his den

examples.zh: 你敢跟他抢生意？这是太岁头上动土！
examples.en: You dare compete with him? You're asking for trouble!

examples.zh: 别在太岁头上动土，小心他报复。
examples.en: Don't provoke him; he'll get his own back.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. 太岁 is a deity associated with Jupiter whose direction was taboo for digging; the saying is also often said 太岁头上动土 alone.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。太岁是与木星相关的神，其方位忌动土；也常只说“太岁头上动土”。

text: 老虎嘴里拔牙——找死
pinyin: lǎo hǔ zuǐ lǐ bá yá —— zhǎo sǐ
literal: tiger · mouth · in · pull out · tooth — seek · death
natural: pulling a tooth from a tiger's mouth

meaning.en: Pulling a tiger's tooth is suicidal; taking a fearful risk, or provoking a dangerous person.
meaning.zh: 去老虎嘴里拔牙，自寻死路；比喻冒极大的风险，或招惹厉害的人。

examples.zh: 跟黑社会讨债，那是老虎嘴里拔牙。
examples.en: Trying to collect debts from gangsters is asking for trouble.

examples.zh: 你这是老虎嘴里拔牙，太危险了。
examples.en: You're playing with fire; it's far too dangerous.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Sometimes said admiringly: 虎口拔牙——胆子不小, 'plucking teeth from a tiger takes courage'.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。有时带赞叹之意：“虎口拔牙——胆子不小”。

text: 老虎戴念珠——假慈悲
pinyin: lǎo hǔ dài niàn zhū —— jiǎ cí bēi
literal: tiger · wear · prayer beads — false · mercy
natural: a tiger wearing prayer beads

meaning.en: A tiger with a Buddhist rosary pretends to be merciful; a cruel person who feigns kindness.
meaning.zh: 老虎戴上佛珠，装作慈悲；比喻凶狠的人假装善良。

examples.zh: 他剥削工人还捐款，老虎戴念珠，假慈悲。
examples.en: He exploits workers and then donates; it's all pretence.

examples.zh: 别被老虎戴念珠的人骗了。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by a ruthless person playing the saint.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Close in meaning to 猫哭老鼠——假慈悲.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。意思与“猫哭老鼠——假慈悲”相近。

text: 脚踩西瓜皮——滑到哪里算哪里
pinyin: jiǎo cǎi xī guā pí —— huá dào nǎ lǐ suàn nǎ lǐ
literal: foot · tread on · watermelon · rind — slide · to · where · count · where
natural: stepping on a watermelon rind: wherever I slide

meaning.en: Slipping on a watermelon rind, one ends up wherever one slides; drifting without a plan.
meaning.zh: 脚踩西瓜皮，滑到哪儿算哪儿；比喻做事没有计划，走一步算一步。

examples.zh: 他对职业规划是脚踩西瓜皮，滑到哪里算哪里。
examples.en: He takes his career as it comes, with no plan.

examples.zh: 做事不能脚踩西瓜皮，要有目标。
examples.en: You can't drift; you need goals.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Often said of an aimless person or approach; sometimes shortened to the second half.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。多形容没有计划、随遇而安的人或做法；后半句有时单用。

text: 木匠吊线——睁只眼，闭只眼
pinyin: mù jiàng diào xiàn —— zhēng zhī yǎn, bì zhī yǎn
literal: carpenter · hang · line — open · one · eye, close · one · eye
natural: a carpenter checking with a plumb line: one eye open, one shut

meaning.en: A carpenter squints with one eye shut to check a straight line; also used for turning a blind eye.
meaning.zh: 木匠吊线时一只眼睁，一只眼闭；比喻对错事装作没看见，不去追究。

examples.zh: 对这点小违规，领导木匠吊线，睁只眼，闭只眼。
examples.en: The boss turned a blind eye to such a small breach.

examples.zh: 别指望他木匠吊线睁只眼闭只眼，他很严格。
examples.en: Don't expect him to look the other way; he's strict.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. In the carpenter's trade the closed eye is for precision; in everyday use it means ignoring faults.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。木匠闭一只眼是为了看得更准；日常用法则指对错误不予追究。

text: 铁拐李的葫芦——不知卖的啥药
pinyin: tiě guǎi lǐ de hú lu —— bù zhī mài de shá yào
literal: Iron-Crutch Li · 's · gourd — not · know · sell · 's · what · medicine
natural: Iron-Crutch Li's gourd: what medicine is he selling?

meaning.en: Nobody knows what remedy Iron-Crutch Li has in his gourd; someone's real plans or motives are a mystery.
meaning.zh: 铁拐李葫芦里卖的什么药没人知道；比喻不知道对方在打什么主意。

examples.zh: 他突然请大家吃饭，铁拐李的葫芦，不知卖的啥药。
examples.en: He suddenly invited everyone to dinner; who knows what he's up to.

examples.zh: 别猜了，他是铁拐李的葫芦，没人知道。
examples.en: Stop guessing; nobody knows what he's got in mind.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Iron-Crutch Li is one of the Eight Immortals, who carries a magic gourd; the standard form is 葫芦里卖的什么药.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。铁拐李是八仙之一，随身带葫芦；通行说法为“葫芦里卖的什么药”。

text: 大风刮倒了帅旗——出师不利
pinyin: dà fēng guā dǎo le shuài qí —— chū shī bù lì
literal: great · wind · blow · down · -ed · commander's · banner — set out · army · not · favourable
natural: a gale knocks down the general's banner

meaning.en: A storm fells the commander's banner as the army marches out; a bad omen at the very start.
meaning.zh: 大风把主帅的旗帜刮倒；比喻一开始就不顺利。

equivalents: get off to a bad start

examples.zh: 新店开张就下暴雨，真是大风刮倒了帅旗。
examples.en: A downpour on opening day; the shop got off to a bad start.

examples.zh: 比赛刚开始就受伤，大风刮倒了帅旗啊。
examples.en: He was injured as soon as the match started.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Used for early setbacks; the second half 出师不利 is also a chengyu.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。形容开局受挫；后半句“出师不利”本身也是成语。

text: 大年三十晚上打兔子——有你不多，没你不少
pinyin: dà nián sān shí wǎn shàng dǎ tù zi —— yǒu nǐ bù duō, méi nǐ bù shǎo
variants: 大年三十逮兔子——有它没它都过年
literal: great · year · thirty · evening · hunt · rabbit — have · you · not · more, lack · you · not · fewer
natural: hunting rabbits on New Year's Eve

meaning.en: On New Year's Eve everyone's busy and nobody cares whether you hunt rabbits; your presence or absence makes no difference.
meaning.zh: 除夕晚上打兔子，打到打不到都一样要过年；比喻有你没你都一样，无足轻重。

equivalents: it makes no difference whether you're there

examples.zh: 你去不去无所谓，大年三十晚上打兔子，有你不多，没你不少。
examples.en: Whether you go or not doesn't matter; you won't be missed.

examples.zh: 在这个团队里，我是大年三十晚上打兔子的角色。
examples.en: In this team I'm someone whose absence wouldn't be noticed.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The first half is often said alone, with a smile, to mean 'you are dispensable'.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。常只说前半句，带调侃意味，表示“可有可无”。

text: 猪八戒的脊梁——悟能（无能）之辈
pinyin: zhū bā jiè de jǐ liáng —— wù néng (wú néng) zhī bèi
literal: Zhu Bajie · 's · back — Wuneng (incompetent) · of · sort
natural: Pigsy's back: the Wuneng (incompetent) crowd

meaning.en: A pun: Pigsy's Buddhist name is Wuneng, which sounds like 无能 (incompetent), and 背 (back) puns on 辈 (sort of person); the saying means a hopeless, useless person.
meaning.zh: 双关：猪八戒法号悟能，谐“无能”；比喻无能的人。

examples.zh: 别指望他，猪八戒的脊梁，悟能之辈。
examples.en: Don't count on him; he's hopeless.

examples.zh: 你这是猪八戒的脊梁，一点本事也没有。
examples.en: You're a good-for-nothing with no skill at all.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. A pun: 悟能 (wùnéng) sounds like 无能 (wúnéng, incompetent). Pigsy's religious name in 《西游记》 is 猪悟能.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。谐音双关：“悟能”与“无能”音近。猪八戒在《西游记》中法号猪悟能。

text: 八字没一撇——还早着呢
pinyin: bā zì méi yī piě —— hái zǎo zhe ne
literal: eight · character · not · one · stroke — still · early · -ing · particle
natural: the character 八 hasn't even its first stroke

meaning.en: The character 八 hasn't even got its first stroke; a matter that has barely started and is far from settled.
meaning.zh: “八”字连第一撇都还没写；比喻事情还没有眉目，离成功还远。

examples.zh: 结婚？八字没一撇呢，你别瞎说。
examples.en: Getting married? It's far too early to say.

examples.zh: 这个项目八字没一撇，先别声张。
examples.en: The project is barely off the ground, so keep it quiet.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The usual form is just 八字还没一撇; 八 is written with two strokes, 撇 and 捺.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。通常说“八字还没一撇”；“八”由撇、捺两笔写成。

text: 吃了熊心豹子胆——胆大包天
pinyin: chī le xióng xīn bào zi dǎn —— dǎn dà bāo tiān
literal: eat · -ed · bear · heart · leopard · gall — gall · big · wrap · sky
natural: having eaten bear's heart and leopard's gall

meaning.en: He must have eaten bear's heart and leopard's gall, to be so daring; extremely bold, usually recklessly so.
meaning.zh: 大概吃了熊的心、豹子的胆，才如此大胆；形容胆子极大，多含贬义。

examples.zh: 你吃了熊心豹子胆，敢顶撞老板！
examples.en: Where did you get the nerve to defy the boss?

examples.zh: 他吃了熊心豹子胆，居然偷到银行去了。
examples.en: He actually had the audacity to steal from a bank.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Bears' hearts and leopards' gall were traditionally thought to make one brave.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。传统上认为吃熊心豹胆能使人胆大。

text: 倒吃甘蔗——节节甜
pinyin: dào chī gān zhè —— jié jié tián
literal: upside-down · eat · sugar cane — joint · joint · sweet
natural: eating sugar cane from the top down

meaning.en: Eating sugarcane from the tip downwards, each joint is sweeter than the last; things getting better and better.
meaning.zh: 从甘蔗梢吃到根，越吃越甜；比喻情况越来越好。

examples.zh: 他们的日子倒吃甘蔗，节节甜。
examples.en: Their life keeps getting sweeter.

examples.zh: 公司业绩倒吃甘蔗，一年比一年好。
examples.en: The company's results improve year after year.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The tip of a sugar cane is the least sweet, so the lower joints taste better.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。甘蔗梢最不甜，根部越来越甜。

text: 大姑娘上轿——头一回
pinyin: dà gū niang shàng jiào —— tóu yī huí
literal: grown · girl · board · sedan chair — first · one · time
natural: a young woman's first sedan-chair ride on her wedding day

meaning.en: A bride rides the bridal sedan chair only once; doing something for the very first time.
meaning.zh: 大姑娘出嫁坐花轿，一辈子头一回；比喻第一次做某事。

examples.zh: 坐飞机我可是大姑娘上轿，头一回。
examples.en: Flying is a first for me.

examples.zh: 第一次上台演讲，大姑娘上轿——头一回，难免紧张。
examples.en: It's my first time on stage, so I'm bound to be nervous.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The traditional bride was carried in a sedan chair; often said to excuse inexperience.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。旧时新娘坐花轿出嫁；常用来为没有经验作解释。

text: 门缝里吹喇叭——名（鸣）声在外
pinyin: mén fèng lǐ chuī lǎ ba —— míng (míng) shēng zài wài
literal: door · crack · in · blow · trumpet — sound (name) · voice · at · outside
natural: blowing a trumpet through a door crack

meaning.en: A trumpet blown through a door crack is heard only outside; a pun on 鸣 (sound) and 名 (name), for being famous abroad, or having a far-reaching reputation.
meaning.zh: 在门缝里吹喇叭，声音传到门外；“鸣”谐“名”，比喻名声在外，传得很远。

examples.zh: 他的大名早就门缝里吹喇叭，名声在外了。
examples.en: His name has long been known far and wide.

examples.zh: 这家小店门缝里吹喇叭，全城闻名。
examples.en: This little shop is famous all over the city.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. A pun: 鸣 (míng, sound) sounds like 名 (míng, name); often used in jest or a touch ironically.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。谐音双关：“鸣”与“名”同音；多作调侃，略带讽刺。

text: 瘸子的屁股——邪（斜）门
pinyin: qué zi de pì gu —— xié (xié) mén
literal: lame person · 's · backside — odd (slanting) · door
natural: a lame man's backside is lopsided

meaning.en: A pun: a lame man's backside tilts (斜), which sounds like 邪 'weird'; something strange, uncanny or irregular.
meaning.zh: 双关：瘸子的屁股是歪斜的；“斜”谐“邪”，比喻事情奇怪、不正常。

examples.zh: 这事真是瘸子的屁股，邪门！
examples.en: This is really weird.

examples.zh: 今天怎么什么都不顺，瘸子的屁股邪门了。
examples.en: Why is everything going wrong today? It's uncanny.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. A pun: 斜 (xié, slanting) sounds like 邪 (xié, odd); rather rude to the disabled, so use lightly.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。谐音双关：“斜”与“邪”同音；对残疾人不够礼貌，宜少用。

text: 老鼠尾巴上长疖子——有脓也不多
pinyin: lǎo shǔ wěi ba shàng zhǎng jiē zi —— yǒu nóng yě bù duō
literal: mouse · tail · on · grow · boil — have · pus · also · not · much
natural: a boil on a mouse's tail

meaning.en: A boil on a mouse's tail contains little pus; something small with little to offer.
meaning.zh: 老鼠尾巴上长疖子，脓也不多；比喻本事、油水或数量有限。

examples.zh: 他那点家底，老鼠尾巴上长疖子，有脓也不多。
examples.en: His savings are meagre.

examples.zh: 让他帮忙吧，老鼠尾巴上长疖子，也出不了多大力。
examples.en: Ask him to help if you like, but he can't do much.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Used of meagre means, ability or gains.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。多形容本领、资财或收益有限。

text: 黄鼠狼下豆鼠——一辈不如一辈
pinyin: huáng shǔ láng xià dòu shǔ —— yī bèi bù rú yī bèi
literal: weasel · give birth to · dormouse — one · generation · not · as good as · one · generation
natural: a weasel bears a dormouse: each generation is smaller

meaning.en: A weasel gives birth to a tiny dormouse; each generation is not as good as the last.
meaning.zh: 黄鼠狼生下的是更小的豆鼠；比喻一代不如一代。

examples.zh: 这几年的新人，黄鼠狼下豆鼠，一辈不如一辈。
examples.en: The newcomers are weaker with each intake.

examples.zh: 老店传到第三代，黄鼠狼下豆鼠，快撑不住了。
examples.en: By the third generation the old shop is struggling.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. 豆鼠 is a very small rodent; the saying belittles the younger generation.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。豆鼠是一种极小的啮齿动物；此语含贬低晚辈之意。

text: 小孩没娘——说来话长
pinyin: xiǎo hái méi niáng —— shuō lái huà cháng
literal: small · child · have no · mother — speak · come · words · long
natural: a child without a mother: a long story

meaning.en: The tale of a motherless child is a long one; it's a long story, hard to explain briefly.
meaning.zh: 孩子没了娘，苦处说不完；比喻事情复杂，一两句话说不清。

examples.zh: 你们怎么认识的？唉，小孩没娘，说来话长。
examples.en: How did you two meet? Ah, it's a long story.

examples.zh: 这事小孩没娘，说来话长，改天再讲。
examples.en: It's a long story; I'll tell you another day.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The second half 说来话长 is the everyday phrase; the first half adds a sad, wry tone.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。后半句“说来话长”是日常用语；前半句增添无奈、辛酸之意。

text: 狗掀门帘——全凭一张嘴
pinyin: gǒu xiān mén lián —— quán píng yī zhāng zuǐ
literal: dog · lift · door curtain — entirely · rely on · one · piece · mouth
natural: a dog nosing aside a door curtain

meaning.en: A dog can only lift the door curtain with its snout; someone who gets by on talk alone, with no real ability.
meaning.zh: 狗只能用嘴掀开门帘；比喻光靠一张嘴说，没有真本事。

examples.zh: 他办事全是狗掀门帘，全凭一张嘴。
examples.en: He relies on talk alone, with no real ability.

examples.zh: 光会说不会做，狗掀门帘啊。
examples.en: All words and no action.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. Mildly insulting; can also mean that someone is a skilled talker.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。略带贬义；有时也指能说会道的人。

text: 雨后送伞——多此一举
pinyin: yǔ hòu sòng sǎn —— duō cǐ yī jǔ
literal: rain · after · send · umbrella — more · this · one · act
natural: delivering an umbrella after the rain

meaning.en: Bringing an umbrella when the rain has stopped; a pointless act, or help that comes too late.
meaning.zh: 雨停了才送伞；比喻做了没用的事，或帮助来得太迟。

equivalents: closing the stable door after the horse has bolted

examples.zh: 事情都办完了你才来帮忙，这是雨后送伞。
examples.en: You turn up to help when it's all done; too little, too late.

examples.zh: 雨后送伞的事，咱们别做。
examples.en: Let's not do something so pointless.

usage.en: Usually only the first half is said, leaving the listener to supply the punchline. Casual and humorous. The same punchline as 脱裤子放屁——多此一举, but milder and more polite.
usage.zh: 多只说前半句，后半句由听者自己领会。口语，带诙谐意味。后半句与“脱裤子放屁——多此一举”相同，但这句更温和、更礼貌。
